newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AMP rules out sale by tender.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AMP rules out sale by tender.

text.p: Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) said on Wednesday it was not considering offering itself for sale by tender as an alternative to demutalisation.
"We are not at this stage thinking of selling the AMP to the Zulus or the Arabs for A$15 billion," AMP chairman Ian Burgess said in an answer to a member's question.
Burgess had been asked if the AMP had considered a sale by public tender in the same way that Scottish Amicable had in Britain.
"It hasn't been suggested to the board as something that might happen in the next month or so," Burgess said.
Burgess said, however, the sale by tender would be one of the options mentioned in the information memorandum proposing demutualisation.
AMP's board expects to consider such a memorandum in July before its planned November 20 members vote.
AMP hopes to list on the Australian and New Zealand stock exchange in the second half of 1998.
